State of Emergency declared for South Carolina ahead of Hurricane Helene
Gov. Henry McMaster issued the executive order
COLUMBIA, S.C. (WBTV) - A State of Emergency was declared for South Carolina on Wednesday, Sept. 25, ahead of Hurricane Helene.
Gov. Henry McMaster issued the executive order as a precaution for the storm’s potential impacts.
“Although South Carolina will likely avoid the brunt of Hurricane Helene’s impacts, the storm is still expected to bring dangerous flooding, high winds, and isolated tornadoes to many parts of the state,” said McMaster.
Related: Flood watches active across Charlotte area with Helene approaching: Here’s where
With a stronger hurricane forecast at landfall, it now appears Helene will remain at hurricane strength well into Georgia, meaning stronger winds for our area.
Widespread heavy rain and gusty winds are expected Thursday night, with peak impacts just in time for the Friday morning commute. Gradual improvement should commence Friday afternoon.
“This State of Emergency ensures that Team South Carolina has the necessary resources in place to respond to these potential impacts,” McMaster continued. “South Carolinians in potentially affected areas should start to take precautions now and monitor local weather forecasts over the next several days.”
Main impacts
Rainfall could total six to 10+ inches in the mountains and foothills from Helene’s rainfall and the rain we’ll see Wednesday before the storm. This has prompted an elevated flooding risk in this area.
Four to six inches of rain are expected in the Charlotte Metro and localized flash flooding will result. Lower rain totals are forecast for the Sandhills.
Related: Hurricane Helene projected to be stronger at landfall: What to know
Wind gusts could reach at least 50 miles per hour in all areas along and west of Interstate 77, downing trees and allowing for scattered to numerous power outages. The highest winds locally are expected Friday morning. Gusts to the east of I-77 could reach 40 mph.
By Friday afternoon, and certainly by this weekend, Helene will have moved out and drier conditions will work in. The weekend will offer highs close to 80 degrees with more sunshine and lower rain chances.
